newsitem.title: India: Indian stocks down for second day in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks down for second day in dull trade.

text.p: ** (1215 GMT) - Indian shares end lower in dull trade
** Benchmark Bombay stocks index dips 6.75 points, or 0.20
** Major foreign funds stay away from the market
** Merrill Lynch says Bombay index likely to rise to
** Delhi index off 1.38 points at 717.18, Madras index loses
13.82 points to 3,253.58 and Calcutta eases 1.0 to
** National exchange index falls 16.50 points to 960.50
A sell-off by speculators in major pivotals forced major Indian bourses to end lower on Tuesday, dealers said.
"There was not much institutional business..fresh selling by speculators dragged down the market..," said a dealer at an institutional brokerage firm.
"Speculators tried to push up prices in mid-session but turned sellers at the close," he added.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top 30-share index rose to an early high of 3,429.37, but ended down at 3,382.74, losing 6.75 points over Monday's close.
